scope: Rails documentation. Optional browser frameworks are not attributed to the server template engine.

ssr.note: Action View renders server templates and layouts.

streaming.note: render stream: true streams the layout and template progressively. Middleware buffering and template constraints apply.

suspense.note: Progressive layout streaming and separately fetched Turbo Frames do not establish a declarative original-response async UI replacement boundary.

client.note: Turbo progressively enhances server HTML navigation and frame/stream updates; this is DOM replacement rather than hydration of a Ruby component tree.
client.label: Turbo / Hotwire

ssg.note: Rendering/caching templates does not establish a complete static HTML site-export workflow.

csr.note: Rails supplies server HTML and integrates optional browser tools; a general component CSR runtime belongs to that selected library.

serverOnly.note: Action View evaluates templates on the server and sends output, keeping Ruby component/template implementations off the browser.

partialRendering.note: Partial templates and fragment caches are not a prebuilt static-shell/request-time dynamic-hole pipeline.

routing.note: The Rails router maps verbs and URLs to controller actions and resource routes.

layouts.note: Layouts wrap views; nested layouts use render/yield composition rather than a filesystem segment hierarchy.

dynamicRoutes.note: Routes expose dynamic segments through params and support constraints.

parallelRoutes.note: The reviewed Rails router does not establish independently navigable named client-route slots.

interceptedRoutes.note: Router resources and controller actions do not establish intercepted-modal/direct-navigation semantics.

prefetch.note: Turbo Drive prefetches eligible hovered links; attributes/events can opt out.
prefetch.label: Turbo Drive

softNavigation.note: Turbo Drive intercepts eligible links/forms, fetches HTML and replaces page content without a full document reload. It maintains browser history and supports permanent elements; apps must follow Turbo's visit lifecycle.
softNavigation.label: Turbo Drive

viewTransitions.note: Turbo Drive can start browser View Transitions when both documents opt in with the view-transition meta tag. CSS controls the animation; unsupported browsers continue ordinary Turbo navigation. Apps must honor reduced-motion preferences.
viewTransitions.label: Turbo Drive

redirects.note: redirect_to/redirect_back issue HTTP redirects; routing can also declare redirects.

serverData.note: Controllers/models load database/application data before rendering Action View.

clientData.note: Turbo Frames request server-rendered fragments and replace matching regions; this is not a browser application query cache.
clientData.label: Turbo Frames

requestDedupe.note: SQL query caching reuses repeated query results within a request. It does not deduplicate arbitrary application HTTP/data loaders.
requestDedupe.label: SQL query cache

persistentCache.note: Rails.cache and fragment caching support configured stores, including Solid Cache.

invalidation.note: Versioned cache keys and dependency-aware fragment caching handle expiration; manual deletion is also available.

isr.note: Fragment/low-level caches and expiry are documented; a static-page export/regeneration contract is not established.

apiRoutes.note: Controllers handle routed HTTP requests and can render JSON responses.

httpErrors.note: Rails maps routing/controller exceptions to HTTP error responses; render status and head let application handlers choose explicit codes. Custom rescue_from handlers must retain the intended status rather than returning a successful-looking error page. Streaming cannot change the status after the response has been committed.
httpErrors.label: Exception mapping / render status

actions.note: Controller actions accept explicit HTTP requests/forms; this is distinct from generated function-call RPC stubs.
actions.label: Controller endpoints

forms.note: Form builders connect model validation, controller submission, and CSRF tokens.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Form builders connect model validation, controller submission, and CSRF tokens.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Rails composes a configurable Rack middleware stack.

cookies.note: Rails supplies signed/encrypted cookie and session mechanisms; security depends on correct application configuration.

cssModules.note: Propshaft fingerprints/publishes assets; CSS Modules compilation belongs to an additional bundler.

scopedCss.note: Action View/Propshaft do not compile component-local CSS selectors; select separate styling/build tooling.

tailwind.note: tailwindcss-rails integrates the Tailwind compiler with Rails asset/build tasks.
tailwind.label: tailwindcss-rails

cssInJs.note: JavaScript styling runtimes and their SSR integrations belong to the chosen UI/bundler stack.

images.note: Active Storage variants resize/transform attached images through configured image processors. This is not arbitrary remote-image optimization.

fonts.note: Font assets can be fingerprinted and served; automatic subsetting and fallback-metric optimization are not established.
fonts.label: Asset files

scripts.note: Asset helpers emit script tags with options; import maps/bundlers integrate browser code. A unified third-party scheduling API is not established.
scripts.label: Asset helpers

assetPipeline.note: Propshaft, included in newly generated Rails apps, fingerprints assets with content digests and generates a manifest. Asset helpers and CSS references resolve to digested URLs. Bundling, compression, and delivery cache headers are separate configuration concerns; files outside the asset pipeline are not automatically versioned.
assetPipeline.label: Propshaft

staticAssets.note: Propshaft fingerprints assets and maps them through a manifest; it is enabled in generated applications.
staticAssets.label: Propshaft

metadata.note: content_for/capture and tag helpers compose authored head markup. A structured SEO metadata-object registry is not established.
metadata.label: View helpers / blocks

dynamicMetadata.note: Controller values and view blocks render request-dependent head tags.
dynamicMetadata.label: Controller / view values

metadataInheritance.note: content_for/yield shares named layout blocks; SEO field merging is application-authored.
metadataInheritance.label: Layout blocks

metadataOverrides.note: content_for can append or flush a named block; this is markup-block replacement, not uniform metadata-field merging.
metadataOverrides.label: content_for flush

titleTemplates.note: Titles can be formatted in view helpers; a dedicated inherited title-template/absolute-title API is not established.

socialImages.note: Attachment image variants do not establish a route-aware generated social-card renderer.

sitemaps.note: Routes can expose XML responses; the reviewed router does not provide automatic crawler sitemap generation.

robots.note: public contains files served as-is, including an application-authored robots.txt.
robots.label: Public file

markdown.note: The reviewed Action View helpers do not establish Markdown parsing/content-page routing.

collections.note: Rendering an Active Record collection is different from a file-content schema/loader/query registry, which is not established here.

draftMode.note: Applications can authenticate previews and bypass caches; a standardized editorial draft mode is not established.

translations.note: Rails ships with the Ruby i18n gem, message lookup, interpolation, and pluralization.

localeRouting.note: The i18n guide documents locale URL parameters, route scopes, and request-scoped locale selection.

localeFormatting.note: I18n.l and locale translation data provide localized date/time formats and related helpers.

auth.note: The authentication generator creates application models/controllers/views for session-based login; it is not a hosted identity provider.
auth.label: Authentication generator

csp.note: A CSP DSL supports global policies, per-resource overrides, and nonces.

cspNonce.note: Rails supplies a configurable nonce generator, nonce directives and script/style tag helpers under its CSP policy. Applications choose a cryptographically random per-response generator and pass nonce values to authored tags.
cspNonce.label: CSP nonce generator / tag helpers

csrf.note: Action Controller forgery protection and form tokens defend configured browser mutation endpoints. API-only apps differ.

environment.note: Environment-specific configuration and encrypted credentials manage server settings; applications control what reaches views.

types.note: The reviewed Ruby/ERB workflow does not establish static component/template-prop type checking. Optional Ruby typing tools are separate.

hmr.note: Development reloads changed Ruby constants per request. Browser component state-preserving hot replacement requires separate tooling.
hmr.label: Server code reload

cli.note: bin/rails provides generators, server, console, tests, and application tasks.

bundleAnalysis.note: Asset fingerprints/manifests do not establish a graphical production module-size analyzer.

unitTests.note: Rails test cases integrate Minitest with model, controller, and integration helpers.

e2eTests.note: System tests integrate browser drivers through Capybara; driver/browser configuration remains separate.
e2eTests.label: System tests / Capybara

observability.note: Rails provides structured request logging, instrumentation, and debugging hooks. External exporters/services add monitoring.

errorHandling.note: rescue_from and exception handling render application error responses; component-local recovery boundaries are not established.
errorHandling.label: Controller rescue / error pages

serverHosting.note: Production Rails applications run a Ruby application server; the guide deploys through the generated production setup.

subpathProxy.note: Rails documents config.relative_url_root or RAILS_RELATIVE_URL_ROOT for deployment beneath a prefix, plus reverse-proxy setup. URL generation, the web server/Rack mount and asset delivery must agree. Configure trusted proxies and the public HTTPS scheme for the deployment rather than assuming every forwarded header is authoritative.
subpathProxy.label: Relative URL root / proxy setup

staticHosting.note: Public assets can be served statically, but dynamic Rails controllers/templates need a Ruby host; complete static-site export is not supplied here.

containers.note: Generated applications include Docker packaging; the deployment walkthrough uses Kamal.
containers.label: Docker / Kamal

edgeHosting.note: The reviewed Docker/server deployment does not establish a worker runtime adapter for Rails SSR.

orm.note: Active Record supplies relational models, associations, validations and a query API.
orm.label: Active Record

assessment.summary: Active Record integrates relationships and eager loading, with strict loading to catch unintended lazy association queries.
strengths: includes/preload/eager_load support different association loading strategies.
Strict loading can expose accidental lazy loads.
tradeoffs: Joins, batching and query behavior differ by strategy/adapter. An ORM checkmark does not promise the absence of N+1 queries.

migrations.note: Versioned migrations apply/roll back schema changes and track schema history through Rails tasks.
migrations.label: Active Record migrations

transactions.note: Active Record transactions group writes atomically and roll back on failure; adapter/database semantics still apply.
transactions.label: Active Record

jobs.note: Active Job supplies queue adapters, dispatch, retries and failure handling. Solid Queue is the default durable backend in new Rails applications.
jobs.label: Active Job / Solid Queue

mail.note: Action Mailer integrates mail templates, delivery configuration and queued delivery through Active Job.
mail.label: Action Mailer

uploads.note: Active Storage attaches uploads to models, manages local/cloud services and supports direct uploads and variants.
uploads.label: Active Storage

realtime.note: Action Cable integrates WebSocket connections, channels and pub/sub adapters with the Rails application.
realtime.label: Action Cable

xssEscaping.note: Action View escapes ordinary output; raw/html_safe marks trusted content and bypasses that encoding. Sanitization helpers are a separate API for user-authored rich HTML.

htmlSanitization.note: Action View sanitize uses the maintained Rails HTML sanitizer with configurable tag/attribute allowlists. Bypassing it with raw/html_safe transfers responsibility to the application.
htmlSanitization.label: Rails HTML sanitizer

authorization.note: Pundit supplies resource policy classes and authorization helpers. Rails authentication and controller callbacks alone do not enforce resource permissions; applications must call the policies consistently.
authorization.label: Pundit

rateLimiting.note: Controller rate_limit defines counts, windows, identity keys and rejection behavior through a cache store. Shared deployment enforcement requires a shared store; this is not enabled for every endpoint automatically.
rateLimiting.label: Controller rate_limit

progressiveEnhancement.note: form_with can emit ordinary server POST forms with authenticity tokens and validation responses. Turbo may enhance delivery; a form that only uses browser handlers must retain a real server submission path.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Native HTML forms

optimisticUi.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific optimistic updates contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

requestCancellation.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific stale request handling contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

typedLinks.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific typed links & parameters contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

stateRestoration.note: Turbo Drive caches page snapshots for restoration visits and supports data-turbo-permanent elements. Snapshots are DOM state, not a guarantee to serialize arbitrary JavaScript state; applications must implement lifecycle cleanup.
stateRestoration.label: Turbo snapshots

scrollRestoration.note: Turbo restoration visits restore the recorded page scroll position. This establishes window/document restoration, not arbitrary nested scrollport state.
scrollRestoration.label: Turbo Drive

navigationBlocking.note: turbo:before-visit can cancel an application visit. This does not intercept every browser history restoration or tab close; beforeunload remains a separate browser mechanism.
navigationBlocking.label: Turbo visit events

navigationAccessibility.note: Turbo documents aria-busy during requests, focus of autofocus elements and updating the document title. It does not promise the same route-announcement/live-region contract as SvelteKit.
navigationAccessibility.label: Turbo focus / busy state

a11yChecks.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessibility checks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

lazyActivation.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific deferred activation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific route / island splitting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

offline.note: The linked deployment API review does not establish the specific offline integration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scheduling.note: Solid Queue recurring tasks use recurring.yml and a scheduler process. Concurrency/deduplication depends on the queue database and retention; do not interpret a recurring schedule as exactly-once execution.
scheduling.label: Solid Queue

notifications.note: Noticed adds notifier objects with per-recipient and bulk delivery methods, including email, ActionCable, push and messaging providers. It uses ActiveJob and persistence; provider credentials, queue workers and delivery/error policy remain deployment/application responsibilities.
notifications.label: Noticed / ActiveJob

searchIndex.note: Searchkick adds model search_data, reindexing and inline, queued, async or manual synchronization with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. It requires a separate search service; association updates are not automatically synchronized and may need explicit reindex callbacks.
searchIndex.label: Searchkick / external search service

fieldEncryption.note: Active Record encrypts declared attributes on persistence and decrypts on reads. Deterministic versus nondeterministic encryption changes query/uniqueness behavior; keys, rotation and storage expansion need configuration.
fieldEncryption.label: Active Record encryption

httpTests.note: ActionDispatch integration tests exercise routing/controllers with session/cookies and response assertions in-process; a real network server is not required. Browser/system tests are separate.
httpTests.label: Integration tests
